newsitem.title: CONGO: French stuck in middle of Congo fighting.
newsitem.headline: French stuck in middle of Congo fighting.

text.p: Some 30 French nationals remained stuck in the heart of Congo's capital Brazzaville as the president's men and a rival militia fought tooth and nail for control.

France's ambassador and his staff, accompanied by gendarmes sent in to protect them and by a few journalists, sheltered in their embassy, just a couple of hundred metres (yards) from the front line and still technically open for business.
A tank from the fragmented army of President Pascal Lissouba fires at the enemy, former leader Denis Sassou Nguesso's militia, from the street outside.
Mortar shells crash into buildings in the area, just beside the Congo river separating what was French Congo from the old Belgian Congo and its capital Kinshasa, in the ex-Zaire of Laurent Kabila.
Shelling and gunfire persisted on Friday, the third day of renewed heavy fighting after a brief ceasefire in the three week old civil war.
Both sides claimed control of the key airport, five km (three miles) from the city centre, but there was no independent confirmation of who was in charge.
The government pleaded for immediate French military help in a letter from its ambassador to the national assembly in Paris.
"If France does not act as rapidly as possible, Congo's democratic regime will live or perish in bloodshed," wrote Pierre-Michel Nguimbi.
Lissouba says Sassou, who led a one-party People's Republic of Congo for 13 years until free elections in 1992, is trying to stage a coup.
Sassou, who runs a private army known as the Cobras, says Lissouba staged the first clash on June 5 as a pretext to prolong his power.
Elections were due on July 27 but have been postponed.
France withdrew 1,250 soldiers from Brazzaville a week ago, has ordered a review of military ties to old African colonies and has declined to join a proposed U.N. peacekeeping force for Congo.
Chances look slim that it would agree to help Lissouba, whose own men assaulted Cesaire -- the only ambassador left here -- and his bodyguard on Wednesday.
Some 1,000 to 3,000 Brazzaville residents have been killed in the fighting and thousands more are fleeing for safety.
Many sought refuge in southern Brazzaville, held by the neutral city mayor Bernard Kolelas, but shelling has caused damage there as well.
